FINDING_ID: LB_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.98  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: `_admissibility_mask()` decides the special `K=1` case from the full `role_map`, not from the actual `self.models` passed into `LoadBalancer`. After failures, `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` passes only active model specs but still passes the old full role map. If only the locked PM remains active, the mask becomes all-zero, `_solve_greedy()` falls back to assigning the PM anyway, and `_check_feasibility()` reports an F3 violation. This is a real boundary bug between role assignment and load balancing.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Build admissibility from the active model list only, or pass a filtered `role_map` aligned to `self.models`; key the singleton rule off `len(self.models) == 1`, not the old role-map size; add a regression test where only PM survives.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `solve()` returns `(Allocation, cost, balanced)` even when HARD feasibility checks fail. It only emits `warnings.warn(...)`, and `_allocation_warnings` never leaves the object. That means callers like `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` cannot tell whether they got a valid plan or an overloaded / role-invalid one. In practice this turns hard allocation failures into soft telemetry.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make infeasibility explicit in the API: either raise on F1/F3 violations or return a structured result containing `feasible`, `violations`, and degradation warnings, and require callers to handle it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.93  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: `_solve_greedy()` does not optimise the stated objective at all. It sorts admissible models only by current load fraction, so ties resolve by input order, not by cost or latency. A verified probe with two identical models showed the solver chose the first model even when it was 10x more expensive, producing cost `100.1` versus an available `10.1`; the same happens with latency when `lambda_lat` dominates.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Choose placements by marginal objective delta rather than raw load fraction, or replace the heuristic with an exact ILP / min-cost flow solver for these small problem sizes.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: Capability-based task matching is missing. `Task.flaw_class` is never used by `LoadBalancer`, and neither `_solve_greedy()` nor `_objective()` uses `CapabilityFingerprint`. So Area 2 does not allocate work based on demonstrated capability, despite `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` claiming that live fingerprints make allocation adapt to observed performance. This is a wrong-ownership split between role assignment and task allocation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add task-model suitability scoring from `flaw_class` and live fingerprints and use it in allocation, or remove the capability-matched allocation claim if that behaviour is not intended.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: `_redundancy_target()` uses `len(self.models)` instead of the number of admissible executors. When `K > 1`, PM is excluded by `_admissibility_mask()`, so a critical task can demand full redundancy `K` even though only `K-1` models are eligible. Verified with `PM + PAR`: target becomes `2`, only `PAR` is assigned, and `_check_feasibility()` still returns success because redundancy shortfall is not checked. Critical tasks can therefore silently miss required coverage.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define redundancy over admissible active executors, or allow PM participation for critical tasks; add an explicit redundancy-feasibility check and surface violations in `solve()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: The real defect also exists upstream of this slice: the caller path feeds `check_dispatch_feasibility()` the wrong budget. `run_exp17_immune.py` and `run_exp12_live_wire.py` pass `len(model_prompt) // 4`, but `experiment_11_orchestrator.py` actually dispatches both system and user messages and reserves output via `max_tokens`. So `feasibility_probability()` is asked about an undercounted load and can approve dispatches that do not fit the true context window.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the raw `task_load` scalar with a shared token-budget helper that includes system prompt, user prompt, and reserved output tokens, and make all callers use it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: When no admissible model can fit a task, the fallback in `_solve_greedy()` force-assigns to `admissible[0]`, which is merely the lowest current load fraction, not the least harmful overload. Verified with `m1=40/100`, `m2=0/10`, and a `70`-token task: the solver overloads `m2` to `70/10` instead of `m1` to `110/100`. That makes already-infeasible plans materially worse than necessary.  
PROPOSED_FIX: If overload is unavoidable, choose the model minimising overflow `max(0, current_load + demand - limit)` with tie-breakers on cost / latency, or run a small repair step before forcing any overload.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
